title.narrative: DRA Innovation - CTP through 121 cash

description.narrative: - streamlining the cash transfer process , with specific attention for local actors by using 121 platform in selected cash projects of JR members. - Creating a better work environment for the implementers by improving the SOPs for cash distributions. - share learnings with all JR local and international JR members to enhance adoption and scaling of 121 within and beyond the JR. - engage FSPs that are not familiar with 121 to integrate with 121 to support scaling in Ethiopia.

Reaching people in need with humanitarian assistance in Ethiopia often still needs quite some time also when cash transfers are used, a modality that is considered as less time- consuming compared to in-kind. The main delays are in lengthy administrative processes needed to register and verify beneficiary lists and sharing those data with the financial service provider that ensures the cash transfer to the beneficiaries. In this process the risk of making mistakes is high. The innovative CVA platform 121 is making the administrative process more (cost-)effective and efficient and will allow a more timely response with less mistakes to the benefit of people affected. This is especially useful also for local partners in the JR that do not have the means to pilot cash innovations and face barriers to keep up with innovations in cash.The administrative cash process is currently mostly done manually in excel files and beneficiary lists are shared with FSP by email, with verifications in email exchanges of lists which is time consuming and risks of mistakes is high which delays the transfers to people affected or reduces effectiveness of response to the costs of beneficiaries in need of assistance.

The cash innovation project will directly target 500 households in North and south Wollo Zone, Amhara region. CORDAID will ensure implemnting partners use strict vulnerability criteria, in line with the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and Clusters guidelines during beneficiary selection process. Special attention will be given to households with girls, women, children under 5, elders and PWDs as they are more vulnerable and disproportionately affected by the conflict. Implementing local partners are expected to use standard vulnerability criteria, and work together with local authorities to ensure the most vulnerable groups are reached.
